newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds hold tight, fretting over jobs.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds hold tight, fretting over jobs.

text.p: *Australian bonds were held to a tight range with sentiment underpinned by the strength of U.S. Treasuries, but with the market reluctant to push higher ahead of Thursday's key data.

Australian bonds were held to a tight range with sentiment underpinned by the strength of U.S. Treasuries, but with the market reluctant to push prices higher ahead of Thursday's key labour force report.

The absence of any notable data until then is likely to see the market keep its subdued appearance, although traders doubt that people will be wanting to go short as a monetary policy easing has yet to be totally ruled out.
U.S. Treasury yields remained at the low levels seen in New York on Monday in early Tokyo trade, having extended the recent rally on hopes the Federal Reserve will hold policy in August.

Continued pressure on the Australian dollar on falling commodity prices, led by gold, and concerns that the Reserve Bank will loosen policy again has yet to impact the debt market, although a further drop could lessen the chances of a rate cut, traders said.
The dollar dropped to an 18-month low of US$0.7420 at one stage in offshore trading.
The September 10-year bond futures contract once again tested its 3-1/2 year peak of 93.210 in SYCOM, although this is proving a stiff barrier after last week steep 30 basis point rally.

The local market's inaction saw it again largely dragging its heels against the dollar bloc. The Canadian market outperformed the U.S. with technical factors helping its 30-year bond yield reach an all-time low on Monday.
